title: Add hub_upload() and hub_delete()
description:
## Summary

hfhub can download from the Hub but not upload. This adds `hub_upload()` and `hub_delete()`, the counterpart to `hub_download()` (the Python `huggingface_hub` has `upload_file` / `upload_folder` / `create_commit`).

Both work over the HTTP(S) LFS protocol, so there is no `git` or `git-lfs` binary dependency. That keeps things consistent with how the rest of the package already talks to the Hub over HTTP.

## What it does

`hub_upload(repo_id, path, ...)` uploads a single file or a whole directory:

1. sha256 each file, then classify it as LFS (size >= 10 MB or a known extension) or inline
2. register the LFS objects through the batch API and upload their bytes to the presigned S3 URLs
   - a single PUT below 5 GB
   - multipart (chunked PUTs, then a complete call) above 5 GB
3. create the commit through the NDJSON `/commit` endpoint; small files ride inline as base64
4. content-addressed dedup comes for free: objects the server already has are skipped

`hub_delete(repo_id, paths, ...)` removes paths through the same commit endpoint.

Both take a `token` (defaulting to `HF_TOKEN`, then `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`, then `HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN`), a `repo_type` (`"model"`, `"dataset"`, or `"space"`), and a `revision`.

Directory uploads include dotfiles, since `.gitattributes` is ordinary repo content on the Hub. Local `.git` metadata is excluded.

## Dependencies

Two changes, and they have different costs, so it is worth separating them.

`jsonlite` moves from Suggests to Imports. It sat in Suggests because the only use was a roxygen example in `hub_download.R`. `upload.R` calls it at six runtime sites: `toJSON` for the LFS batch body, the multipart completion body and the NDJSON commit lines, `fromJSON` for the batch and commit responses, and `base64_enc` for inline files. Installed weight does not change either way, because httr already imports jsonlite, so it is on every hfhub user's machine already. This is just an honest declaration of what the code now does at runtime.

`digest` is the one genuinely new package, and it is here for a measured reason. It computes the LFS oid, and LFS files are routinely multi-GB, so the hash has to stream rather than buffer. openssl would have been free, since httr imports that too, and it returns a byte-identical sha256. But it buffers: on a 1 GB file it peaks around 349 MB RSS, against 66 MB for digest, and digest stays flat as the file grows while openssl does not. Hashing a 20 GB checkpoint is the normal case here, so the extra dependency buys bounded memory.

No new system dependency either way. It is all httr/curl, no git-lfs.

## Testing

Unit tests cover token resolution, the no-token error, repo-type mapping, multipart part ordering, LFS batch error handling, the empty-input guards, and the dotfile/`.git` split. 30 tests, `R CMD check` clean.

A live upload+delete round-trip exercises both an inline file and an LFS file (a tiny `.safetensors`, which is LFS by extension), verifies the committed oid against a local hash, and cleans up after itself. It is gated on `HFHUB_TEST_UPLOAD_REPO` plus a write token, so it skips on CRAN and in CI without credentials.

I also validated it out of band by uploading a 2.5 GB model (three safetensors shards plus a config) to a dataset repo and reading it back with a matching oid, and by forcing the multipart path on a 40 MB file (3 chunks) with the same round-trip check.

## Fixes since the first version

Two bugs in the LFS path, both silent:

- **Multipart part ordering.** Part URLs arrive as header names `"1".."N"` and were ordered with `sort()`, which is lexicographic: `1, 10, 11, 12, 2, ...`. The chunks are read sequentially from the connection, so from the second chunk onward each one was PUT to the wrong presigned URL and labelled with the wrong `partNumber`. It only goes wrong past 10 parts, which is exactly why the 3-chunk validation above did not catch it. Ordering is numeric now, split into a helper so it is covered by a test with 12 synthetic parts and no bytes uploaded.
- **LFS batch errors read as dedup.** The batch reply reports per-object failures in `error`, and a failed object carries no `actions` either. Treating a missing upload action as "the server already has it" turned a rejection into a silent skip, and the commit then referenced an oid that was never stored. Errors abort now; a missing action without an error still means dedup.

Smaller ones in the same pass: `hub_upload()` and `hub_delete()` refuse empty inputs rather than posting a header-only NDJSON body (which the Hub takes as an empty commit); directory uploads stopped dropping dotfiles; and the live round-trip registers its cleanup immediately after upload, so a failed assertion no longer leaves the test directory behind on a real repo.

## Notes

- The LFS response uses the `application/vnd.git-lfs+json` content type, which httr does not auto-parse, so it is decoded explicitly with jsonlite.
- Multipart parts are held one chunk at a time (default 16 MB from the server), so memory stays bounded for large files.

title: Windows symlinks
description:
On Windows, creating symlinks requires either administrator privileges or developer mode. When these aren't available, `hub_download()` fails silently:
- Files download successfully to `blobs/`
- `file.symlink()` fails and returns `FALSE`
- Warnings are generated but ignored
- `snapshots/` directory remains empty
- Applications can't find model files

This PR fixes the problem by putting the files directly in snapshots when `file.symlink()` fails. This is less space efficient when there are multiple snapshots for a model, but it does work.

The Python huggingface_hub implementation has similar behavior to this.

title: Add HF_TOKEN support and improve gated repo error messages
description:
## Summary

- Add `HF_TOKEN` as the primary environment variable for authentication (it's the standard used by HuggingFace CLI and Python libraries)
- Provide helpful error messages for gated repos and auth failures

## Changes

1. **HF_TOKEN support**: Check `HF_TOKEN` first, then fall back to `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN` and `HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN`

2. **Better error messages**:
   - **GatedRepo (403)**: Instructs user to visit the model page and accept the license
   - **Unauthorized (401)**: Instructs user to set HF_TOKEN and provides link to token settings
   - **Other errors**: Shows the error message from HuggingFace API

## Example error output

Before:
```
Error: Distant resource does not seem to be on huggingface.co (missing commit header).
```

After:
```
Error: Access denied to gated repository.
ℹ This model requires accepting a license agreement.
ℹ Visit <https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-3-12b-it> to accept the terms.
ℹ Make sure you are logged in with the account that owns your HF_TOKEN.
```

## Testing

Tested with `google/gemma-3-12b-it` (a gated model requiring license acceptance).
